title: One-step decrement behavior
statement: Let $P$ be a counter program on input $x$, let $\ell,\ell'$ be labels, let $\rho$ be register values, and let $p$ be the input read position. If the instruction at $\ell$ is to decrement register $r$ and continue at $\ell'$, then for every current output string $o$ there is a run of at most one step from label $\ell$, registers $\rho$, read position $p$, and output $o$ to label $\ell'$, with register $r$ decreased by one with zero truncated at zero, all other registers unchanged, the same read position, and output still $o$.
hypotheses_covered: Instruction at $\ell$ is the decrement of $r$ followed by $\ell'$
replaced:
Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$, $r$ a register and $\ell$ a
label whose instruction is $\mathsf{dec}(r, \ell')$.  Then for all registers
$\rho$ and input positions $p$, from label $\ell$ with registers $\rho$ and $p$
symbols read the program reaches label $\ell'$ within one step, printing
nothing, with $p$ symbols read and registers $\rho$ except that register $r$ now
holds $\max(\rho(r) - 1, 0)$.
